title.narrative: Svenska Röda Korset: Påverkansarbete för Migranters rättigheter
Swedish Red Cross: Advocating for Migrants' Rights

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the project "Advocating for migrants' rights and dignity", implemented by the Swedish Red Cross and the Red Cross Migration Network in Latin America, is that the rights of women, children and men who migrate are bolstered in line with international humanitarian and human rights legislation.
This overall objective is underpinned by two specific outcomes:
Outcome 1: A stronger regional migration network with increased coordination and capacity to advocate for migrants rights.
Outcome 2: Improved inclusion of migrants voices, needs and rights in national and regional decision making.

Detta projekt gäller stöd till Svenska Röda Korset för projektet Advocating for migrants’ rights and dignity under treårsperioden 2024-2026. Den totala budgeten är 10 MSEK och Sida är enda givare till projektet. Det övergripande målet är att stärka rättigheter, i linje med internationell humanitär rätt och konventioner om mänskliga rättigheter, för kvinnor, barn och män som migrerar Projektets förväntade resultat är: - Ett starkare regionalt migrationsnätverk inom Röda Korsrörelsen med ökad samordning och kapacitet att verka för migranters rättigheter. - Att migranters röster, behov och rättigheter inkluderas i nationellt och regionalt beslutsfattande som rör dem. Svenska Röda Korset genomför projektet i samarbete med det regionala migrationsnätverk som består av tolv nationella Röda Korsföreningar i Latinamerika. Colombianska Röda Korset har rollen som sekretariat för nätverket. Projektet syftar till att driva och stärka påverkansarbete och humanitär diplomati inom Röda Korsets regionala nätverk för migration och därigenom säkerställa att kvinnor, barn och män som migrerar kan åtnjuta sina rättigheter i enlighet med humanitär rätt och MR-lagstiftning. För att uppnå detta kommer nätverket tillvarata erfarenheter och främja möjligheter till deltagande för kvinnor, barn och män som migrerar. Projektet kommer att samverka med lokala migrantorganisationer för att gemensamt identifiera de behov och rättigheter som drivs gentemot beslutsfattare och för gemensamt deltagande i påverkansarbete. Medlemmarna i nätverket kommer, tillsammans med migrantorganisationer och andra humanitära aktörer, att försöka påverka nationella lagar och regionala policyer till stöd för migranters rättigheter tillgång till viktiga samhällstjänster. Ett evidensbaserat narrativ kommer att utvecklas för att möjliggöra och stärka ett koordinerat påverkansarbete gentemot regeringar för att påverka lagar, policyer och praxis av vikt för migranters rättigheter. Genom detta förväntas uppnås en bättre förståelse hos beslutsfattare för migranters behov och utmaningar under hela migrationsprocessen. Myndigheter kommer att erinras om det ansvar som åligger dem för att bidra till att migranter kan åtnjuta sina rättigheter och ges skydd. Förutom dessa prioriteringar kommer nätverket att förespråka hållbara lösningar, såsom lokal integration, migranters tillgång till grundläggande samhällstjänster, sysselsättning, familjeåterförening och säker rättslig status, såväl utifrån lokala kontexter som med ett regionalt perspektiv. Lösningar och positiva narrativ kring migration kommer att utformas och drivas för att bidra till ökad inkludering som främjar migranters möjligheter att bidra till samhällsutveckling. Det regionala migrationsnätverket kommer att få stöd och stärkas genom tillgång till såväl verktyg som kapacitetsutveckling för arbetet med humanitär diplomati. Projektet förväntas har störst inflytande i norra Sydamerika och Centralamerika, samtidigt som det regionala perspektivet är av vikt.

This project Advocating for migrants’ rights and dignity is implemented by the Swedish Red Cross during 2024- 2026 with a budget of 10 MSEK. The overall objective is that the rights of women, children and men who migrate are bolstered in line with international humanitarian and human rights legislation. This overall objective is underpinned by two specific outcomes: - A stronger regional migration network with increased coordination and capacity to advocate for migrants’ rights. - Improved inclusion of migrants’ voices, needs and rights in national and regional decision-making. The Swedish Red Cross implement the project together with the regional migration network composed by twelve Red Cross National Societies in Latin America. The Colombian Red Cross host the secretariat for the network. The project will advance and strengthen the advocacy and humanitarian diplomacy efforts of the Red Cross regional network for migration to ensure that migrants can enjoy their rights in accordance with humanitarian and human rights law. The migrants themselves are an integral part of the project and the project will seek to capture their experiences and pressing needs in each territory. The project will also involve local migrant organizations to identify needs and rights to be advocated for towards decision-makers, as well as for participation in advocacy roundtable-discussions. Together with migrant organizations and other humanitarian actors, the members of the network will advocate towards decision-makers and seek to influence national laws and regional policies to support migrants’ rights as well as their safe and effective access to essential services. An evidence-based narrative will be developed to enable meaningful, coordinated engagement with governments and influence migration-related laws, policies and practice. The aim is to enable a better understanding by decision-makers of migrants’ needs and challenges throughout migratory routes, recalling authorities of their responsibilities, including measures to protect migrants. These are key priorities as well as advocating for sustainable solutions, such as local integration, access to basic services, employment, family reunification and secure legal status, based on local experiences and promoting a regional perspective. Solutions and positive narratives around migration will be promoted to enhance the inclusion of, and enable women, children and men who migrate the opportunities to contribute to the development of society. The network will be supported and strengthened through tools-, skills- and capacity development in humanitarian diplomacy. While pursuing a regional approach, the project will have the greatest influence in Northern South America and Central America.

description.narrative:
An initial result from the first year is the setup of a solid project structure and development of a baseline. In the beginning of 2024, a steering group was established consisting of representatives from the Colombian and Swedish Red Cross, ICRC and IFRC with the main purpose of following the implementation, ensuring its adherence to the intended plan and discussing strategic pathways. A working group consisting of nine national Red Cross societies (Colombia, Honduras, Panama, Mexico, Ecuador, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Grenada, Trinidad & Tobago) in the region has also been established with the intention of steering the project in accordance with regional migration priorities.
All activities have been executed as planned apart from the regional meeting which was postponed from the end of 2024 to the beginning of 2025 in order to better take into account the learnings from an evaluation of the Red Cross regional migration action plan and combine the project with the formal establishment of Red Cross Regional Migration Network in Latin America.
Below are examples of initial results of activities during the first year related to each outcome objective.
Outcome 1. A stronger regional migration network with increased coordination and capacity to advocate for migrants rights: The regional focus of the project has allowed for improved coordination among the national Red Cross societies in the region, leading towards more efficient work, less duplication of efforts and more effective support towards the migrant population. The increased coordination has strengthened the formulation of joint and evidence based advocacy messages. A physical meeting in September 2024 gathered humanitarian diplomacy and migration focal points from nine national societies currently participating in the network to promote coordination, participation, and identify necessary capacity development.
The knowledge of the national Red Cross societies on migration issues, policies, and legal frameworks has been strengthened. A data collection tool has been developed to enable analysis of stakeholders, policies and legal frameworks in the selected geographical areas. A forthcoming challenge in the region not foreseen when the project was initiated is the downsizing of other actors due to financial restrictions and its impact on data collection etc. Hence, the red Cross Movement needs to strengthen data collection and not only rely on other partners.
A digital training in humanitarian diplomacy in relation to migration has been produced, and will be launched in 2025, expected to enhance technical capacities, guidance and knowledge.
To develop and strengthen the links between what is done regionally to the global level and enable anchoring of issues beyond the project the Swedish and Colombian Red Cross participated in a leadership meeting in Geneva, in conjunction with the Red Cross Movement's statutory meetings, and gave a joint speech in relation to the launch of the Movements Global Migration Strategy.
For its advocacy actions the network prioritized access to health, dignified transportation conditions, disappearance, and stalking by human trafficking networks as issues to strengthen humanitarian diplomacy actions. A benefit from working through the network is that individual members who may not be able to voice concerns nationally can still express matters through collective actions on a regional and international level.
A final, but important, result for this outcome is that the project has enabled the formalization of the Red Cross Regional Migration Network including a secretariat function, with an ambition for the network to enhance its ability to advocate and become financially independent. A somewhat unexpected results is increased involvement of other national Red Cross societies in Europe who have committed to supporting the network in various ways, both technically and financially.
Outcome 2. Improved inclusion of migrants voices, needs and rights in national and regional decision making: Through a mapping of migrant organizations in the region, the project identified a total of one hundred and ten (110) key organizations and designed a methodology for approaching these organizations through interviews and focus groups. The coordination with migrant organizations aims to strengthen the involvement of migrants in the project and ensure their perspectives are laying the foundation for evidence based humanitarian diplomacy.
In focus group discussions the participants highlighted work, health and education as the main barriers related to their rights. Furthermore, that migrant women and gender diverse individuals face severe risks, including gender based violence and exploitation. Some of the key messages brought forward from these meetings by network members in different fora include the importance of policies addressing these vulnerabilities and promote gender equality. Additionally, the Movement publishes reports and case studies that highlight migrants' experiences, using these documents to advocate for better policies and practices at national and international levels.
The network and its members participated in several key spaces, among them the Ministerial Meeting of the Cartagena 40 Process including the national thematic consultations. This provided a good opportunity for the network and its members to increase participation in key events, establish new working methods, improved coordination and to position the Red Cross as an actor that adds value. The systematization of the focus group meetings with migrant organizations were key for the interventions of the network delegates in these fora. Based on the national consultations and the ministerial meeting in Chile, key commitments were established that reflect the importance of the participation of migrant organizations and national Red Cross societies in the region.
Another example is migrant organizations in Colombia invited the Colombian Red Cross to participate in a public hearing that analyzed and debated the State's response and the role of civil organizations within the context of the 2024 Venezuelan presidential elections. The hearing was attended by various state entities with competences in migration, including the Ministries of Foreign Affairs and of Interior and 15 migrant organizations. In its intervention, the Colombian Red Cross emphasized among other the humanitarian concerns of the Network due to changes in migration policies evident in the region, including the return of migrants and funding cuts.
While the national Red Cross societies has often been seen primarily as a health and disaster risk management organization, this project is expanding the recognition of its role in humanitarian assistance and diplomacy in migration contexts.
